scope.summary: This standard covers the requirements of solid drawn (seamless) copper and copper alloy tubes of outside diameters 5 mm to 80 mm, both inclusive, for use in condensers and heat exchangers.

revision_history.edition: Third Revision (revised to refine geometric definitions, update chemical compositions and mechanical properties, make edgewise bending optional, and include straightness tolerances)

version_status_and_amendments.amendment_slips: No active amendments have been issued since the publication of this third revision copy.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Metallurgical Engineering / Industrial Heat Transfer)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Copper Products (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all solid drawn copper and copper alloy tubes used in condensers and heat exchangers must conform to IS 1545:1994 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Large-scale enterprises had to comply by October 19, 2024, small enterprises by January 19, 2025, and micro enterprises by April 19, 2025. Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified tubes is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Exemption is granted solely for export-oriented shipments. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial copper alloy tubes.

requirements.detail: Every packaging box containing tubes must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to certify compliance.
Applies to solid drawn (seamless) tubes with nominal outside diameters ranging from 5 mm to 80 mm (inclusive). Wall thickness and outside diameter dimensions and tolerances must conform to IS 5493.

As an alternative to the standard hydrostatic pressure test, each tube must be tested to a minimum internal air pressure of 35 N/cm² (approximately 3.5 bar) for a minimum period of 5 seconds. The entire length of the tube must be immersed in water during testing, showing zero bubbles or signs of leakage.

For tubes supplied in Temper Annealed (TA) and Annealed (O) conditions only, longitudinal samples must show uniform and complete recrystallization when examined under a magnification of 75x per IS 4748. The average grain size must lie strictly between 0.010 mm and 0.050 mm, with the maximum grain size not exceeding 0.050 mm.

For TA and O condition tubes, by mutual agreement, a stress-corrosion test is conducted using ammonia vapor. A 150 mm length tube specimen is degreased, pickled in a 10% sulphuric acid solution, washed, and dried. It is suspended in a closed desiccator above an ammonium chloride solution adjusted to pH 10 using sodium hydroxide flakes. After 24 hours of exposure, it is pickled lightly and examined for any signs of cracking. Cracking at sawn ends is ignored.
Alternatively, a stress-corrosion test can be conducted in accordance with IS 2305 : 1988 using a mercurous nitrate solution. The specimen must show zero signs of chemical cracking.

One test must be conducted from each lot for: a) Tensile properties (tested per IS 2655); b) Hardness properties (Vickers tested per IS 1501); c) Flattening properties (tested per IS 2328); d) Drift expanding properties (tested per IS 2335) to verify wall ductility and flare capability without splitting.
The inner and outer surfaces of the tubes must be clean, bright, smooth, and completely free from harmful defects such as severe scratches, cracks, inclusions, pitting, or oxidation scale.

To prevent physical bending, rubbing, and surface damage during transport, the tubes must be suitably covered with polyethylene sheets and packed with proper plastic inserts at the ends. The gross weight of each packaging box must not exceed 1,000 kg, and the bottom of the packing cases must be completely rigid to maintain perfect straightness.

requirements.requirement_type: Scale of Sampling and Lot Definition
requirements.detail: A lot comprises up to 300 tubes or 1,000 kg (whichever is higher) of the same grade, size, thickness, and condition. Ten tubes are drawn at random for visual/dimensional checks (zero defectives allowed). If the lot passes dimensions, one sample is tested for chemical, mechanical, flattening, and drift expanding tests, and one sample for microscopic examination.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 1545 : 1994 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing solid drawn (seamless) copper and copper alloy tubes (from 5 mm to 80 mm outside diameter) designed for industrial condensers, coolers, and heat exchangers. Formulated under India's statutory Copper Products Quality Control Order (QCO), all such condenser-duty tubes supplied to the Indian market must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to ensure maximum thermal conductivity, pressure integrity, and corrosion resistance. It specifies seven standard alloy grades—including pure deoxidized copper, arsenical brasses (Admiralty and Aluminium brass), and high-durability cupronickels—supplied in five physical tempers. The standard enforces detailed quality testing, including 100% non-destructive eddy-current scans, standard hydrostatic/pneumatic leak tests at 3.5 bar, tight microstructural grain boundaries (0.010 to 0.050 mm) for annealed tempers, mechanical deformation audits (flattening and drift expansion), and stress-corrosion cracking tests to prevent sudden tube failure under harsh operating fluids.
